arguments.title: Freight Export Data-Quality Audit
arguments.spec:
# Freight Export Data-Quality Audit (analysis, not a build job)

`input/shipments.csv` (312 data rows) and `input/carriers.csv` are READ-ONLY evidence. Do not clean, repair, or
edit anything under `input/`. Both are plain CSV: a header row, then data rows, no quoted fields, no embedded
commas. Row numbers are 1-based over the DATA rows (the first row after the header is row 1).

Deliverable `analysis/data-quality.json` (starts `{"schemaVersion":1,"complete":false,"violations":[]}`):
`violations` holds one entry per rule the dataset actually breaks (not one per offending row), each
`{rule, column, count, exampleRows, why}`. `count` is the exact offending-row count, recomputed from the data --
not an estimate. `exampleRows` cites at least two distinct offending 1-based row numbers. `why` explains what the
violation costs a consumer, at least twelve characters. A rule with zero offending rows must NOT get an entry.

Four rules only -- a defect outside them is out of scope and must not be reported, because an unrecognised rule
name fails the check:
- `duplicate_primary_key` (column `shipment_id`): its `shipment_id` occurs more than once in the file. every such
  row counts toward `count` -- an id used three times contributes three rows, not one.
- `out_of_range` (column `weight_kg`): numeric weight outside `0 < weight_kg <= 30000`. A non-numeric/blank
  `weight_kg` is not counted under this rule -- there is no separate rule for it.
- `wrong_type` (column `delivered_at`): the cell is non-empty and is not a full ISO-8601 UTC instant
  `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`. An empty cell is legitimate (not delivered yet) and is never a violation.
- `referential_break` (column `carrier_id`): its `carrier_id` is not one of the ids in `input/carriers.csv`.

Frozen: `input/`, everything under `test/`, and `scripts/run-tests.mjs` are evidence, not workspace -- `npm test`
recomputes their content digests each run and fails if any moved. `test/data-quality.test.js` DERIVES its truth
from both CSVs each run (it stores no counts, no row numbers), so re-deriving the numbers yourself IS the work; a
number you have not actually computed fails the suite immediately.

Set `complete` true only once every rule the dataset actually violates already has a violation entry recorded --
coverage is checked only at that point, and the failure message names any rule still missing.

Toolchain: the sandbox is OFFLINE. Never add a dependency or test framework; the declared acceptance command
(`npm test`) must pass exactly as-is with the fixture's own toolchain.
arguments.plan:
Five sequential cards, one shared deliverable file (`analysis/data-quality.json`) -- ordered so each
card starts from the previous card's committed result instead of racing it as a parallel sibling:

1. record-duplicate-primary-key -- compute and record the `duplicate_primary_key` violation, if any.
2. record-out-of-range (after 1) -- compute and record `out_of_range`, if any.
3. record-wrong-type (after 2) -- compute and record `wrong_type`, if any.
4. record-referential-break (after 3) -- compute and record `referential_break`, if any.
5. finalize-completeness (after 4) -- independently re-confirm every violated rule is recorded, then set
   `complete: true`, verified by two real `npm test` runs (before and after the flip).

Each rule card: read the deliverable fresh, run `npm test` for real to confirm the current green baseline, write a
throwaway scratch script (kept out of `input/`) that parses the CSV(s) directly per the rule's exact predicate,
append exactly one violation entry if the count is nonzero (or add nothing if it is zero), then rerun `npm test`
to confirm still green. No card touches another rule's entry or the frozen evidence paths.
arguments.summary: Splits the freight data-quality audit into one card per rule (duplicate shipment ids, out-of-range weight, malformed delivered_at timestamps, unknown carrier ids) plus a final completeness pass, run in sequence so they safely append to the one shared JSON report instead of racing each other. 5 cards total. Assumption: each rule card computes its own count from the raw CSVs with a scratch script rather than trusting any other card's numbers, per the spec's 'recompute, don't estimate' rule.

Checklist:
- Build the actual workflow first; avoid landing-page patterns, ornamental cards, and explanatory feature text inside the app.
- Keep operational screens quiet, dense, scannable, and predictable. Cards are for repeated items, modals, or framed tools, not page sections.
- Use existing primitives: `Button`, `Dialog`, `AlertDialog`, `Tooltip`, `Spinner`, `Kbd`, and `cn` from `src/components/ui/`.
- Use Lucide icons in icon buttons, Radix for headless controls, and Tailwind v4 utilities over custom CSS.
- Preserve the always-dark theme. Use tokens such as `bg-surface-0`, `bg-surface-1`, `bg-surface-2`, `text-text-primary`, `text-text-secondary`, `border-border`, and `text-accent`.
- Make mobile and desktop text fit without overlap. Keep fixed-format controls dimensionally stable.
